D013-D008_h001.question:
For about five months now, I’ve felt like I’ve been walking around with a weight on my chest. Most days I just feel…flat or really low, like there’s no point in anything. I feel like I’m a burden to my wife and our kids, like they’d honestly be better off if I wasn’t around. I’ve thought a lot about ending it. I’ve gone as far as picking a spot out on a remote job site, thinking I could “fall” from a roof or make it look like an accident with the harness. I’ve gone over the timing, how I’d make sure no one was nearby.

This feels different from those times when I was up for days, talking fast, starting big projects, and feeling unstoppable. This is the opposite—like I’ve crashed and can’t get back up. It’s gotten bad enough that I’m missing jobs and my boss has warned me.

    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D013-D008_h002.question:
For about five months now, it’s like something inside me is just…gone. I don’t feel sad exactly, more like hollow, like I’m watching my own life from the outside. I go to the office or log in from home to handle claims, but I just stare at the screen. I’m constantly restless—pacing around the house, rubbing my hands, picking at my cuticles until they bleed. I can’t sit through a whole phone call without getting up and walking around.

I keep replaying tiny mistakes at work, like miskeying a number, and I feel like I’ve ruined someone’s life. If a claim is delayed, I’m convinced it’s my fault and that I deserve to be punished. At night I lie there thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up—not that I have a plan, just this wish to disappear.

This feels especially jarring because a few years ago I had this spell where I didn’t sleep for days, felt wired and unstoppable, talking fast, starting huge projects, spending way too much money. My husband was worried then; now he says I’m the opposite—barely functioning, withdrawing from everything.

D013-D008_h003.question:

I feel kind of dead inside most of the time—like I’m watching my life instead of living it. Customers yell, my boss rides me, and I just… don’t feel anything, or it’s all muffled.

I’m convinced that bad things that happen are somehow my fault. When there was that pile-up on the highway last month, I kept thinking it happened because I had wished I didn’t have to go into work that day. It sounds crazy when I say it out loud, but it feels real.

Sometimes I get these sudden urges to step into traffic when I’m crossing the street, or to jump off the parking garage at the mall. They hit me out of nowhere and scare me.

This feels different from that time a couple years ago when I went days with almost no sleep, felt unstoppable, was talking a mile a minute, spending way too much money, and thought I was destined to start some huge business empire.
